transcript.text: The plastic catch on my Hotpoint dryer door has snapped and now the door won't stay shut so it won't start. Model TVFM70BGP. Can I just get a new catch?

Yes, in most cases you can. On most dryers like yours the door catch is a separate plastic part that clips or screws into the door, and it's a common owner fix. The dryer won't start because the catch is what holds the door against the door switch. With the catch gone the switch never closes, so the machine thinks the door is open. That's the safety interlock doing its job, not a second fault. 1. With the dryer switched off and unplugged, look at the door edge. If the plastic tongue or hook on the door is snapped, that's the door catch, the simplest and cheapest repair.
2. If that's cracked, or there are bits of broken plastic stuck inside, it can stop even a new catch engaging. On many dryers the door switch sits behind that slot, so damage there can mean the switch or receiver needs attention too.
3. Open and close the door gently and check it lines up squarely with the slot, and that the hinges aren't loose or dropped. A door that sits off-line strains the catch and can snap a new one before long. If only the door catch is broken and the slot looks fine, a new catch should sort it. If the receiver or switch area is damaged too, that changes what's needed. Please don't tape or wedge the door shut, or try to force the switch, to get it running. The interlock is there for a reason. One other thing worth doing: Hotpoint (and its sister brands) ran a large safety modification programme on many vented and condenser dryers, and your model may be in it. It's worth entering your model and serial number on Hotpoint's dryer safety checker, or checking GOV.UK product safety alerts. If it's affected, follow their instructions before using it again, and they may be able to help while it's being looked at. Which part has actually snapped: the hook on the door, or the slot it clicks into?

It's the plastic tongue on the door that's snapped off, I found it on the floor. The slot in the cabinet looks fine. There's a green dot on the door frame too, so it was modified in 2017. Do you know the part number for the new catch?

I can't give you a reliable part number, sorry. Hotpoint often uses different parts for the same model code depending on the production run, so a number I quote could easily be the wrong one. The safe way to find the right catch is to use the full details on the dryer's rating label, usually inside the door rim or on the back. That means the model code plus the service or serial number. Enter them on Hotpoint's own spares site or a reputable UK spares supplier and search for "door catch" (sometimes listed as "door latch" or "door hook"). Check the photo matches your broken piece before going further. Holding the snapped tongue next to the picture is the easiest way to be sure. With the tongue snapped off and the slot undamaged, the broken catch is probably the whole reason it won't start. The door switch can't close without it, so I'd treat the catch as the fault, and I'm fairly confident of that. The green dot is reassuring, because it shows the 2017 modification was done on your machine. 1. Look at where the old catch was fixed to the inner door. If there's a stub held by one or two screws or clips, it's a straightforward swap. If the fixing point in the door itself is cracked, a new catch may not hold, and the door part may need attention too.
2. Close the door slowly and watch the old stub line up with the slot. If the door sits low or off-centre, the hinges may be loose. Gently tightening them while unplugged helps the new catch last. If the door clicks shut firmly with a new catch but the dryer still won't start, the door switch behind the slot would be the next suspect.
Ok, I'll check the label inside the door. I'll unplug it before fitting anything, no burning smell or anything, it's just the latch. Do you want the service/serial number as well as the model?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
No need to send it to me. I can't look up exact part numbers, so it wouldn't change my advice. But do keep the service/serial number to hand when you order, because that's what tells a spares listing which version of the door catch your dryer takes. Write down both the model code and the service number from the label. Everything you've found points to the door catch. That's a mechanical break, not an electrical fault, and I'm confident a new catch will get it starting again. On some dryers the tongue is sold as part of a door handle/catch assembly rather than on its own, so don't be surprised if the listing shows a slightly bigger piece. A matching part for your model is shown below. 1. The model code and service number on the listing match your rating label.
2. When fitting, keep it unplugged and fit the catch with the door open. Then close the door gently and make sure it clicks firmly into the slot before you press start. That last one would point to the door switch behind the slot, which needs the cabinet opening up.
